note: v2479: The last of the nine review findings. Four were the same failure: a guard that reads for a TOKEN is satisfied by the token, not by the mechanism. test_dom_probes scar-1 assertion was a pure tautology - it uppercased the source, renamed the functions OWN name __leafText to SKIP, then found SKIP - so deleting the tag filter outright left all 11 tests green while the walker read script source as screen text. test_fleet_routes checked the token SUBJ appeared somewhere, so restoring the hardcoded the chronicles while leaving var SUBJ declared-and-unused shipped the photographed FLEET defect, green. Both now RUN the code in node and judge what it produces. test_app_ctx_nav extracted its condition from raw source while stripping comments only from the resolved text, so a comment inside the if satisfied it. And a refused tally painted all three fleet lanes DARK blaming the wire for a failure the board had already explained; it now reads UNKNOWN and quotes the boards own reason. Also corrected: my prune_wilson docstring told the reader main() is the only module-level call in control_app. It is not - 119 calls run outside the guard and importing the console DOES write to disk. The true and narrower claim is that it does not start the DELETER.
